title: Choose starting-state and prove reset deliberately
when: Before scheduling QA that resets a host
need: A dedicated baseline needs golden capture plus restore proof, not just SSH or a saved archive. Verify/reset are destructive provisioning operations. Each Test Machine chain declares its starting baseline and resets before its head. Explicit inherit keeps that chain's state for a follower. Capacity-machine registration is separate from test-machine registration. A nonzero native baseline probe retains its diagnosed quota, authentication, model or transport cause. If the requested baseline fails during mission preparation, the refusal surfaces the recorded probe reason, recovery and exit code when available. Quota and unknown failures preserve the golden and do not justify sign-in or credential resets; authentication recovery needs actual native evidence. Reset keeps the identity store (~/.yoke-browser-identities) and harness logins live outside goldens, never restores stale sign-in state from an older golden, and closes identity browsers before clearing so their cookies are on disk. Require separate real reset and browser sign-in proof against the selected release. On Ubuntu24.04, Codex sandbox recovery audits the actual denied executable, grants userns only to that exact helper while retaining the global restriction at1, and requires ordinary sandbox command exit0/output in the same desktop-opened session plus fresh audit inspection. Re-audit after helper updates; renewed denial or missing helper blocks provisioning. To verify a predecessor's files in the same chain, record stable hashes in method_config.continuity_fingerprint on the inheriting case; the runner refuses continuity_lost before setup or mission walking if the files cannot be proven. macOS restore retries a failed captured-entry copy once; a persistent failure retains its named restore receipt.
surface: Per-OS capture/verify/reset; machine setting optional baseline; Pack starting-state contract. Current Linux golden-home reference and Machine QA Linux baseline capture/recovery procedure.
gap: The entry guide must explain when a resettable rig is necessary. Do not make every browser user build a clean-install lab or mistake capacity registration for QA readiness.
review: Pending exact live recipe proof. YOK-5406 source replaces the earlier snap Chromium and Safari carry-forward with the reset-kept identity store; real reset/sign-in and released proof remain pending. Scoped sandbox recovery has producer-reported actual proof on requirement 49008, QA run 50474, artifacts 36760 and 36761: same-session ordinary sandbox command exit0/output, scoped profile and global sysctl1. This proves that recovery only; overall installer and released recipe proof remain pending. A later api.upyoke.com DNS restriction is a separate blocker, not an AppArmor failure.
